experiment_contract.authority_boundary: Experiment metadata and finite computation are evidence, not proof authority; claim status changes only through Lean, an exact counterexample, or the named owner verifier.

problem.target_statement: Prove that the Erdős #68 factorial-denominator series is irrational.
problem.claim_ceiling: Erdős #68 remains open. Lean checks the support-independent channel congruence and LCM obstruction, the finite factorial-gap segment inequalities and explicit radius lower bounds, summability and additivity of every finite-support channel residual, and the complete prime-unit translator giving exact integer residual shifts. Lean also checks the strict-successor carry recurrence, its exact normalized factorial-series expansion, and convergence of the normalized strict successors Z_n/n! to the literal series S. Consequently S is non-irrational exactly when the carries are eventually all one, and S is irrational exactly when non-unit carries occur cofinally. This is an exact characterization, not the missing producer. An independently implemented exact GMP certificate computes every carry through m=300000; combined with the Lean-checked consumer, its non-unit terminal carry proves only the finite bound q>=300000 for any displayed rational representation S=a/q with q>0. The source-verified Erdős--Straus Theorem 2.1 coboundary criterion applies to the checked ordinary-factorial carry expansion, not directly to denominators n!-1. Lean checks the criterion's small-numerator hypothesis from the sharp carry range, proves that every corresponding half-radix coboundary enters the canonical interval -B<c_m<=0, and proves that the finite residue state then hits zero at a large multiple of B and stays zero. Thus the entire Erdős--Straus route is formally reduced back to eventual unit carries rather than producing a distinct irrationality obstruction. The source-verified Kovač--Tao interval lemma, together with a Lean-checked exact overlap inequality, gives a rational comparison series after decreasing each denominator n!-1 by at most n^2+1; this is a sharp perturbation boundary, not a result on the unperturbed endpoint. The source-verified Li Lai Theorem 1.1 supplies, after f=-1 specialization, a positive-lower-density family of n with P(n!-1)>(1+9 log 2-epsilon)n. Lean promotes least such prime hits to cofinally many uniquely supported upper-half anchors on explicit tailored blocks [2,2p-1]: prefix privacy handles all earlier indices and the prime cannot divide the immediately following factorial gap. Lean also proves the one-owner weighted projection is nonzero automatically. However, any one-owner closing inequality would force (2p+1)L_p<2p^2((2p-1)!)^2, while the source-verified Garaev--Luca--Shparlinski Theorem 12 yields the derived growth log L_p >> p^(4/3)log p, eventually exceeding that squared-factorial ceiling. Thus unique support is abundant but the one-owner route is asymptotically impossible; the eventual source-to-ceiling comparison is not Lean-checked. The source-verified Luca--Shparlinski Lemmas 4-5 now add exact prime and general-modulus hit bounds; for q=p^a they control reuse by O((x-y)log x/(a log p)+1), and their final remark controls aggregate p-adic load. Those are unweighted collision estimates, not weighted endpoint residue information. The componentwise denominator dynamics now prove a sharper multiplicity law: if q divides the repeated-birth cofactor B_n and ord_q(R_n)>ord_q(C_n), then ord_q(n!-1)<=ord_q(v_n); hence every genuinely amplifying repeated prime with ord_q(v_n)<ord_q(n!-1) enters C_(n+1) with its complete current-gap power. The canonical product A_n of all such full powers divides B_n, C_(n+1), and the next actual denominator v_(n+1); when nontrivial it also carries a nonzero next-numerator projection. This confines cancellation beyond old residual mass to non-amplifying q-adic collisions, but no source theorem yet supplies cofinally large A_n or bounds the exceptional mass. Lean further checks the uniform remote factorial-grid construction for every cutoff and threshold: its normalized augmented matrix is a shifted Vandermonde with nonzero determinant, Cramer's rule supplies a zero-channel vector with nonzero moment, and a remote prime translator reduces the residual to absolute value at most 1/2. Every Cramer tail numerator is an exact row-replacement determinant and is nonzero beyond the largest support. The full infinite-tail classification is now formal: R_D(c)=M(c)T_D+K universally, and under zero channels R_D(c)=M(c)S+K for the original series S; for the uniform Cramer kernel M(c)=det(A) is nonzero. Direct uniform tail-sign and total-positivity closure are false because nonaffine floor quotients force sign changes inside the finite pre-asymptotic tail. The global CRT route now has a Lean-checked fractional-part normal form: T_p/R_p=C_p*s_(2p-1), gcd(T_p,R_p)=1, and the normalized complementary residue is exactly the gap from C_p*s_(2p-1) to its next integer. A full unit-carry block p<=m<=2p forces the same endpoint window, so every collision-ceiling certificate now yields an exact failure of m | strictFacTopRat(factorialGapPrefix(m),m) somewhere in that block; cofinal certificates land directly in the exact cofinal miss predicate equivalent to the problem. The exact recurrence probe now explains all three observed private-owner transitions as the first block containing the exited prime's first later factorial-one hit, opening a cofinal two-owner renewal target rather than another blind horizon extension. Lean also splits a unit carry exactly into a lower zero-digit endpoint cylinder and an upper maximal-digit endpoint cylinder. Therefore it suffices to prove cofinal prime escape from only the lower cylinder m*theta_(m-1)<R_m, whose width is R_m/m=O(m^-2); rationality would force theta_(p-1)=0 for every sufficiently large prime. This sharper cofinal escape producer is still unproved for the actual series. No theorem proves that renewal supply, cylinder escape, cofinally many exact misses, the required global/two-projection bound, or det(A)S nonintegral for an unbounded family, so no irrationality resolution is claimed. The tail-free predecessor-gap certificate has now been evaluated for the first time: it fires for 204 of 208 values of m up to 210, with a failure count within 10% of the uniform prediction and no failures past m = 60. The producer's event is therefore generic, and its missing input is a non-concentration theorem for frac((m-1)! sum_(n<m) 1/(n!-1)) rather than a new arithmetic mechanism. The tail-free threshold producer, the exact prefix strict-successor miss, and the canonical-digit lane are now identified as three level sets of the single rounding digit D_m over 3<=m<=50000, with the digit statistically indistinguishable from generic on every tested statistic, so the surviving Archimedean input is one non-concentration statement for A_(m-1) at scale 1/m rather than three separate producers. The finite denominator exclusion is now a Kempner-index statement: a non-unit carry at m gives q not dividing (m-1)!, hence q not dividing 299999! from the landed certificate, which is strictly stronger than the previously recorded q>=300000. The finite denominator exclusion is now two independent statements: q does not divide 299999!, which kills every 299999-smooth denominator of any magnitude, and q > 10^12039 from 23449 certified continued-fraction partial quotients. Neither implies the other and the recorded q >= 300000 is superseded by both.

hypothesis.statement: The finite denominator exclusion recorded for this problem is close to what finite computation can give, so improving it needs new machinery.

probe.question: How large a denominator can be excluded for S = sum_(n>=2) 1/(n!-1) by a continued-fraction prefix whose every quotient is forced by a rigorous rational bracket, and do the certified quotients look generic?
probe.computation: Bracket S by exact integers lo <= 2^B S <= hi, run the interval continued fraction so a quotient is emitted only when both endpoints agree on it, and read the bound off the last certified convergent via best approximation of the second kind, checking |q_n S - p_n| > 0 against the bracket rather than assuming it. The arithmetic self-checks against the known expansion of e and the convergents of pi before every run.
probe.falsifier: A bound not far exceeding the recorded exclusion, which would mean the recorded one was already near best; or an anomalously large partial quotient, which would place S unusually close to a rational and hand over a concrete candidate denominator to test.
probe.stop_condition: A bound many orders of magnitude past the recorded one, with generic Levy and Gauss-Kuzmin statistics, settles the question and leaves nothing further for this route.

analytic_bridge.survival_consequence: The recorded exclusion stands as near-best and finite denominator work needs genuinely new machinery.
analytic_bridge.falsification_consequence: The recorded exclusion was far from best and this standard route, absent from the packet, replaces it.

result.summary: 23449 certified partial quotients at B=80000 bits give q >= 2^39991, above 10^12039, with the separation |q_n S - p_n| > 0 verified against the bracket. The recorded exclusion was q >= 300000, from a 300000-index GMP carry certificate. It does not subsume the Kempner-index exclusion and is not ranked against it: q not dividing 299999! kills every 299999-smooth denominator of any magnitude while saying nothing about size, and this bound says nothing about smoothness. The certified quotients are generic: Levy's constant matched to 0.38 percent, Gauss-Kuzmin worst |z| = 1.97 over the first five values, largest partial quotient 35923, and -- the coordinate that actually matters -- a maximum irrationality exponent witness of 2.00099 over convergent denominators above 2^10000. So there is no anomalous near-rational and no candidate denominator to hand back to the problem's own machinery.

progress.decision_basis: Every quotient is forced by the bracket, the separation is verified rather than assumed, and the arithmetic reproduces the known expansions of e and pi.
progress.next_analytic_target: None from this route: the expansion is generic, so no larger partial quotient and no Liouville-flavoured candidate denominator is available. Finite denominator exclusion is not on the path to the cofinal statement.
progress.authority_boundary: This classification routes research attention; it does not promote finite evidence to proof authority.

mechanism_bindings.rationale: Replaces the recorded finite denominator exclusion with one many orders of magnitude stronger by a standard route the packet did not contain, and records that the expansion is generic so the route is now exhausted.
